GraphOptions

GraphOptions configures the graph created by new Graph(options) and requires container and data.

PropertyDescriptionTypeDefault
containerRequired. Mounts the canvas. Pass a CSS selector or a mounted element with nonzero dimensions. See the container requirements.string | HTMLElement—
dataRequired. Supplies nodes, edges, and optional Combo groups. Pass { nodes: [], edges: [] } for an empty graph.GraphData—
autoFitControls whether to refit the view when the container resizes. See setSize().boolean | number or FitViewOptionsfalse
labelControls label scaling and hides labels at low zoom or on collision. Set text and appearance in node.style and edge.style.LabelOptionsDefault scaling and visibility policies
nodeSets node shapes, appearance, state styles, labels, and decorations.NodeConfigcircle with theme and built-in styles
edgeSets edge shapes, line styles, arrowheads, labels, and state styles.EdgeConfigline with theme and built-in styles
comboSets the appearance, labels, and collapsed shapes of all Combos. Define membership through data.combos and each node's comboId.ComboConfigDefault Combo styles
layoutSets the algorithm and parameters used to position nodes.LayoutConfigExisting x and y, with missing axes set to 0
behaviorsConfigures interactions such as zoom, drag, and selection. An explicit array replaces the defaults. Pass [] to disable all behaviors.BehaviorOption[]['zoom-canvas', 'drag-canvas']
transformsEnables custom transforms or parallel edge separation.TransformOption[]—
pluginsConfigures registered plugins to mount in the graph container.PluginOption[]No plugins
themeSets default colors and other style values for the canvas, nodes, edges, and states.ThemeOption'light'

autoFit / FitViewOptions

autoFit: false preserves the view on resize. true uses a fit factor of 0.9, and a positive number sets the factor directly. An object accepts the fields below. The first render fits the view.

PropertyDescriptionTypeDefault
paddingUniform padding or top, right, bottom, and left values in CSS pixels.number | [number, number, number, number]0
minZoomMinimum zoom when fitting.number0.1
maxZoomMaximum zoom when fitting.number20

Caution

Use distinct IDs for nodes, edges, and Combos, and keep them stable across updates. Edges reference existing nodes, and Combo parent relationships must be acyclic.

GraphEdge

GraphEdge describes one edge connecting two nodes in data.edges.

PropertyDescriptionTypeDefault

targetRequired. Target node ID.string—

Matching source and target creates a self-loop. Edges with distinct IDs can share endpoints. See parallel edges and self-loops.

edge controls shapes, lines, arrows, labels, and selected styles.

PropertyDescriptionTypeDefault
typeEdge type or a registered extension name.'line' | 'arc' | 'polyline' | 'cubic' | string'line'

EdgeConfig.style

EdgeStyleValue<T> accepts a value or a (source, target, edge) => T function.

PropertyDescriptionTypeDefault
strokeEdge and arrow colorEdgeStyleValue<string>theme.edgeStroke; light '#99ADD1', dark '#637088'
lineWidthVisual width; use a finite positive valueEdgeStyleValue<number>theme.edgeLineWidth, preset 1
opacityOpacity from 0 to 1EdgeStyleValue<number>1
lineDashEmpty means solid; the current period uses the sum of the first two values, as described in Dash rulesEdgeStyleValue<number[]>[]
startArrowSource-end arrow pointing toward sourceEdgeStyleValue<boolean>false
endArrowTarget-end arrow pointing toward targetEdgeStyleValue<boolean>theme.edgeArrow, true in both light and dark
arrowSizeLength along the path; use a finite positive explicit length. Nonpositive values use automatic lengthEdgeStyleValue<number>Derived from line width
hitAreaWidthTotal picking width, independent of visual width; see Picking widthEdgeStyleValue<number>Final lineWidth

Use finite nonnegative numbers for the first two entries in lineDash. Their sum determines the period, with half stroke and half gap. With fewer than two entries or a zero sum, the edge is solid. Set lineWidth > 1 to ensure dashes render on built-in straight edges. Gaps remain pickable and arrowheads stay solid.

hitAreaWidth is the total width across both sides of the edge, in screen pixels. Its minimum is the current visual width. Omitted, negative, and nonfinite values fall back to the visual width.

ParallelEdgesConfig

edge.parallelEdges and process-parallel-edges use these fields.

PropertyDescriptionTypeDefault
enabledExplicitly enable the object entry or supply the transform. Setting the edge option to false disables both entries.booleanfalse
offsetOffset step in graph coordinates. Values other than finite positive numbers fall back to 20.number20
mergeByGrouping uses both endpoints, including when a subset or empty array is supplied.Array<'source' | 'target'>['source', 'target']
includeReverseGroups A→B with B→A. Setting it to false groups the directions separately, so two single reverse edges may overlap.booleantrue
minOffsetMinimum absolute offset for an edge away from the center. Values other than finite nonnegative numbers fall back to 0.number0
maxOffsetMaximum absolute offset. Values other than finite nonnegative numbers fall back to 80.number80

The edge array determines offset order. Each offset is (index - (count - 1) / 2) * offset, with its magnitude clamped to minOffset and maxOffset. The center offset stays 0. Edges at the cap can overlap, and adding, removing, or reordering edges recomputes offsets.

line edges use arc paths in groups with multiple edges. With separation enabled, arc uses the group’s curvature, with 0 for single-edge groups. cubic, polyline, and self-loops use their own paths.

Fields resolve in this order from lowest to highest priority: built-in defaults, the last matching object transform’s options, and the edge.parallelEdges object. A string transform enables separation. To turn separation off, set edge.parallelEdges to false or { enabled: false }. parallelEdges: true retains transform options.

combo.style sets the default appearance of all groups, with data.combos[].style available for per-group overrides.

Nesting, collapsing, and changing membership at runtime remain experimental and may change within 0.1.x. Collapsing hides descendant nodes and their edges.

Combo bounds are computed from node shapes and child combo outlines. Labels do not contribute to bounds. Expanded labels scale up to 1.5 times their configured size and are hidden below 6 screen pixels. Global label settings for nodes and edges do not apply to combo labels.

PropertyDescriptionTypeDefault

For the same state, per-combo styles override global styles. The 2-screen-pixel fallback outline for selected takes priority over the 1.5-pixel fallback for active or highlight. An explicit selected style replaces its fallback. Setting either active or highlight replaces the fallback for both. Set styles explicitly for disabled and inactive. Only built-in states take part in style merging.

LayoutConfig

layout computes node positions and, when omitted, uses the input x and y with missing coordinates defaulting to 0.

Common options

PropertyDescriptionTypeDefault
typeRequired. A built-in or registered layout name, such as 'dagre' or 'grid'. Unknown names use random placement. Register optional layouts before use.string—
workerSet to false to disable. See the layout guide for execution order and fallback behavior.booleanGraph attempts to use a Worker by default at 1,000 nodes or more
widthWidth used for layout computation.numberCurrent canvas width

width, height, and center use graph coordinates. Graph uses the canvas dimensions in CSS pixels as the default layout width and height. mindmap, indented, and fishbone use their own sizing and spacing options.

Tree layouts

The same tree can appear as a mind map, an indented list, or a fishbone diagram. Declare nodes in nodes and express each parent-to-child relationship as an edge from source to target. Use a connected tree with one root.

LayoutPreviewWhen to use it
Mind map mindmapBranches extend to either side of the central topicOrganize several branches around a topic.
Indented tree indentedNodes occupy separate rows, with children indented below their parentsShow a file directory, menu, or category hierarchy.
Fishbone diagram fishboneCategories attach to the spine, with items arranged along the branchesShow a problem, categories of causes, and individual causes.

Switch layouts in the canvas to compare how they arrange the same data. When creating a graph, pass the chosen layout. For indented trees and fishbone diagrams, also set the matching polyline router in edge.

Mind map (mindmap)

Branches extend horizontally from a central topic. This example uses ID prefixes to keep A and C and their descendants on the left, and B and D and their descendants on the right. Extra space around first-level branches keeps leaves from overlapping.

nodeGapVertical gap between adjacent children on the same side.number30

getHeightGets the node height.(node: GraphNode) => numberReturns 40

Layout options

Set the layout type and its options in layout. For example, layout: { type: 'dagre', rankdir: 'LR' } arranges a flow from left to right.

Layout typeExample optionsEffect
Hierarchical dagrerankdir: 'LR', nodesep: 32, ranksep: 80Arranges layers left to right, with 32 units between nodes in a layer and 80 between layers.
Grid gridcols: 4Arranges nodes in four columns. Use rows to set the row count.
Circular circularradius: 120Places nodes on a circle with a radius of 120 units.
Concentric concentricsortBy: 'degree'Places nodes with more connections closer to the center.
Radial radialfocusNode: 'A', unitRadius: 60Centers the rings on the node with ID A, with 60 units between rings.
Force-directed force, d3-forcelinkDistance: 100Aims to place directly connected nodes 100 units apart.
force-atlas2kr: 8, kg: 2Higher kr pushes nodes farther apart. Higher kg pulls them toward the center.
fruchtermangravity: 12Higher gravity pulls nodes closer to the center.
mdslinkDistance: 80Uses 80 units as the target distance between directly connected nodes.
Random randomwidth: 800, height: 600, center: [400, 300]Places nodes randomly inside an 800 × 600 area centered on [400, 300].

Detailed options and interaction rules

Navigation and dragging

PropertyDescriptionTypeDefault
zoom-canvas.sensitivityMultiplier for the normalized wheel-delta percentage.number1
zoom-canvas.minZoomMinimum wheel zoom factor.number0.1
zoom-canvas.maxZoomMaximum wheel zoom factor.number20
drag-canvas.ignoreModifierKeysLeaves drag gestures with Shift, Ctrl, or Meta for brush or lasso selection.booleantrue

All three zoom options require finite positive numbers; invalid individual values use their defaults. If the resulting minZoom ≥ maxZoom, all three options reset to defaults. Same-direction wheel events merge within a frame, opposite direction replaces pending input, and each frame is capped at 15%. Line deltas multiply by 16, page deltas by canvas CSS height. Bounds constrain wheel behavior, not programmatic zoomBy or fitView.

drag-node starts after more than 3 client pixels of left-button movement. It does not rerun layout, and a later layout can overwrite moved positions. drag-edge starts on a hit edge, choosing the nearer endpoint, target on ties. It emits edge:dragstart/drag/dragend. A dragend reconnected result proposes a valid node drop; it does not indicate changed data. Apply endpoints through application data and public methods such as setData. Use the batch form of updateEdgeData() to change source and target.

Selection

PropertyDescriptionTypeDefault
click-select.multipleWhen enabled, hold trigger while clicking to append to the selection.booleanfalse
click-select.triggerModifier for appending to the selection. 'ctrl' maps to Ctrl and 'meta' to Meta.shift / ctrl / meta'shift'
brush-select.keyModifier for brush selection. null needs no modifier, and 'ctrl' accepts Ctrl or Meta.'shift' | 'ctrl' | nullnull
brush-select.throttleMsDeclared in the type. Graph uses a 100 ms interval and finalizes on release.number—
lasso-select.keyModifier for lasso selection. null needs no modifier, and 'ctrl' accepts Ctrl or Meta.'shift' | 'ctrl' | nullnull
lasso-select.throttleMsDeclared in the type. Graph uses a 100 ms interval and finalizes on release.number—

click-select toggles an already selected element off. Clicking an unselected element without the append modifier clears node and edge selections first; empty canvas clears them too. It does not select Combos.

Brush starts on non-node surfaces (canvas, edge, Combo) and tests node centers. Each update replaces all node selected states, without clearing edges. Lasso clears only nodes from its own previous selection, retaining selections from other sources; at least three samples form a valid polygon. Do not bind both area-selection behaviors to the same gesture.

Area selection emits brush:select/end or lasso:select/end rather than per-node node:selectchange. select is emitted for nonempty results; end can return empty nodeIds. Listening only to node:selectchange misses other selection sources.

Highlighting

PropertyDescriptionTypeDefault
hover-highlight.degreeNeighbor traversal depth. Use a finite nonnegative integer. The current implementation uses the supplied value.number1
hover-highlight.inactiveStateDimming state for other elements. A common choice is 'inactive' with corresponding node and edge state styles.string—

highlight-node and highlight-edge control renderer emphasis without writing highlight states. hover-highlight writes highlight and optional inactiveState, cleans up its tracked states on leave, and freezes hover during node/Combo dragging.

degree controls neighbor traversal, but directly incident edges and endpoints are always included, so degree: 0 does not isolate the hovered node. Enabling both built-in highlight-node + highlight-edge combines them into hover-highlight; state effects differ from using either alone. Prefer hover-highlight directly instead of stacking overlapping hover behaviors.

delay uses browser timer semantics and offset does not validate finiteness. Prefer finite values and nonnegative delay. Default text uses textContent; custom strings use innerHTML, so escape untrusted values or return an HTMLElement populated with textContent. No visual skin is provided, and pointer-events is none. Use an application overlay for clickable content.

Custom interaction contract

MemberSignatureContract
Optional init(context: ExtensionContext, options: Readonly<TOptions>) => voidoptions includes type; Readonly is a type constraint, not runtime freezing on this path
Required getEvents() => BehaviorEventHandlers<TEventMap>Partial event-to-function map, automatically bound and unbound
Optional destroy() => voidClean up owned DOM, listeners, timers, and asynchronous tasks

BehaviorExtension<TOptions extends BehaviorOptions = BehaviorConfig, TEventMap extends object = GraphEventMap>. BehaviorEventHandlers maps each event argument tuple to a handler. destroy has zero arguments. Applications can call graph.emit() to invoke custom handlers. Augment GraphEventMap to check emitted arguments and infer listener parameter types. See the custom event example.

Pass a factory that returns a fresh instance directly to register(). The lifecycle is create → init → getEvents → destroy. There is no promised update hook; remounting destroys and recreates instances. Registry replacement does not immediately replace mounted instances.

Creation, init, getEvents, and handler synchronous errors are isolated and logged with behavior/phase details. Handle asynchronous rejections yourself. Use context.data/state/viewport, requestRender, and isDestroyed; do not write through snapshots or depend on internal renderer/eventEmitter or deprecated context.graph. See Custom interactions for implementation and cleanup.

ThemeOption

theme sets the default canvas and element appearance through a built-in theme and optional style overrides.

ValueEffect
'light' / 'dark'Built-in light and dark themes. Defaults to 'light'.
{ type, ...tokens }Select a base theme, then override values such as colors and sizes.
PropertyDescriptionTypeDefault
typeRequired. Base preset for object entries. Omitting theme uses 'light'.'light' | 'dark'—

Objects require type; all tokens are optional fixed values, without callbacks. Resolution starts from the preset and replaces top-level fields. Explicit undefined overwrites a preset value; omit fields you do not need to change.

ThemeTokens

Built-in defaults follow. Units and valid values match the corresponding node styles and edge styles; theme resolution adds no numeric validation or normalization.

Both presets define edgeStroke, so changing only edgeDefaultColor does not change default edge colors. Themes have no label, icon, or Combo tokens; configure those styles separately.

Complete category palettes

light: ['#1783FF', '#00C9C9', '#F08F56', '#D580FF', '#7863FF', '#DB9D0D', '#60C42D', '#FF80CA', '#2491B3', '#17C76F'].

For category colors, read edgeCategoryPalette from resolveTheme and map business categories to colors in a function assigned to edge.style.stroke. Setting the palette alone does not recolor edges.

State presets

The node emphasis outline is #163B65 in light and #B7D3FF in dark. Only overridden fields are listed below.

StatenodeStateStylesedgeStateStyles
activehaloWidth: 8, opacity: 1stroke: #1783FF, opacity: 1
selectedstroke: emphasis, strokeWidth: 2, haloWidth: 12, opacity: 1stroke: #1783FF, opacity: 1
disabledopacity: 0.15opacity: 0.15, lineDash: [4, 4]
highlightstroke: emphasis, strokeWidth: 1, opacity: 1stroke: #1783FF, opacity: 1
inactiveopacity: 0.25opacity: 0.25

See node state styles and edge state styles for supported fields. The renderer hides hidden directly and skips overrides for default. Multiple states apply in list order; later states overwrite the same fields. An active node gets halo 8 when its halo is 0; selected has a minimum halo of 12. haloWidth: 0 cannot disable these built-in effects.

Theme guide

Theme precedence and runtime updates

Code and rendered result

Choose light, dark, or brand. Default uses base theme styles; Selected and Disabled use state styles. The brand theme preserves other preset node states. Label colors are updated separately on each switch.

See the example canvas for this section.

Precedence

For field-object base styles: explicit node/edge.style fields > registered extension defaults > theme tokens > renderer fallbacks. Whole-object node style functions use a compatibility path with different defaults and state handling; see Style functions.

State styles apply after base styles. For each state, the renderer chooses the object from node/edge.stateStyles, then extension state styles, then theme state styles. Once an object is chosen, missing fields are not filled from lower levels. An empty object also suppresses the theme override for that state.

Preserving preset state styles

A theme's nodeStateStyles or edgeStateStyles replaces the entire preset map. Spread both levels to keep other states and other fields within the same state:

resolveTheme

Resolve tokens from the preset and overrides in ThemeOption. To apply a theme to an existing graph, use updateOptions.

Accepts ThemeOption and returns ThemeTokens. Fields remain optional in the public type; account for undefined when reading them. The function creates a top-level object and copies the palette array; state maps and nested objects are not deeply cloned. Treat results as read-only and construct new state objects using spreads, rather than mutating shared objects.

Runtime updates

graph.updateOptions({ theme: nextTheme }) replaces the entire previous theme option and refreshes styles. It does not accumulate previous custom tokens, rerun layout, or call fitView.

Switching from { type: 'light', nodeSize: 36 } to 'dark' restores default node size 24; explicit node.style.size still wins. Construct a complete nextTheme to retain brand tokens. The application must synchronize label colors, page backgrounds, and system dark mode separately.

Continue with Themes, Graph.updateOptions, or Default themes and states.

TransformOption[]

Custom transforms process the full input in array order before layout. The built-in process-parallel-edges computes edge offsets after the graph data is applied. See the Transforms for configuration examples.

PropertyDescriptionTypeDefault
typeRequired. Transform name for object entries. You can also pass a registered name or process-parallel-edges directly.string—
optionsRegistered transforms define their own options. The built-in transform uses ParallelEdgesConfig.Record<string, unknown> | ParallelEdgesConfig{}

Usage example

Rendered result

The transform adds a prefix to node labels.

Transform options

GraphOptions.transforms?: TransformOption[] defaults to no registered transformations. Each entry is a string or an object with type and optional options. options is Record<string, unknown>; the special parallel-edge entry also accepts ParallelEdgesConfig.

This is configuration only. Register app-normalize as TransformExtension with beforeRender. String form sends to init / update; object form sends only options, excluding the outer type. Do not put prefix on the outer object.

Entries execute in order before layout. The same name at two positions has two instances. A later render / setData reuses the same position/name and calls update with complete options, not a diff. Removal or name changes release old instances.

process-parallel-edges is a built-in special case that does not invoke a registered Transform. See parallel-edge options for fields, disabling, and precedence over the transform entry.

PluginOption[]

plugins enables registered plugins and mounts them in the graph container.

PropertyDescriptionTypeDefault
typeRequired. Registered plugin name.string—
[key: string]Plugin-specific options passed as top-level fields.unknown—

Extension guide

Plugin options and extension lifecycle

GraphOptions.plugins?: PluginOption[] defaults to empty. Every entry is an object with type: string; other top-level fields are business options. PluginOptions<TType> can constrain names and fields. There is no string shorthand.

Register app-counter as PluginExtension. init receives the whole object, including type and caption. A nested options object is not automatically flattened. mount receives the Graph DOM container. Repeated same-named entries instantiate separately; names are not deduplicated.

Calls and changes

OperationRegistered TransformPlugin
First renderCreate, init, transform inputCreate, init, mount
Repeated renderReuse matching position/name; update then transformDestroy old instance; create and mount again
setDataTransform new input, then layoutDoes not remount
layout / incremental writesDo not rerun registered transformsDo not remount
Graph.destroyDestroy current instancesDestroy; release plugin-owned resources

Changing Transform or Plugin configuration requires a new Graph. Replace behaviors independently with setBehaviors().

Options and support boundaries

Extensions validate their own options; fields do not acquire engine meaning merely by appearing in GraphOptions. Build instance state from current values and defaults in init / update. Do not mutate received read-only options.

Registered Transforms return GraphData synchronously, not a Promise. Plugins own asynchronous completion, cancellation, and errors. Unknown names are skipped rather than activated. See runtime contracts for errors/cleanup and registration for isolation.

Runtime changes

After creation, use updateOptions() for styles and interactions. Replace data with setData(), or change layout with setLayout() and layout().

After the first render completes, use updateOptions() to update nodes, edges, labels, the theme, or interactions. Earlier calls throw. Calls after destruction return immediately.

OptionMerge rule
node, edgeShallow-merge top-level fields and keep omitted fields.
node.styleMerge fields when both values are objects. If either value is a style function, replace the entire value.
edge.styleMerge object fields.
node.stateStyles, edge.stateStylesReplace the entire state map. Pass a complete map to keep other states.
labelShallow-merge top-level fields.
themeReplace the whole option, then resolve the preset.
behaviorsPassing an array replaces the entire list. Omit it or pass undefined to keep the current list. Pass [] to disable all behaviors.

You can also change interactions with setBehaviors(). Use data mutations for data and Combos and setLayout() and layout() for layout. Create a Graph with new options to change the container, autoFit, plugins, or transforms.
